defective_pattern: Taking a shortpath by copying a plaintext Markdown file into a .docx extension (e.g., cp .md .docx) instead of generating a true binary OpenXML document.
why_defective: A .docx file is a zipped XML binary (OpenXML). Copying raw plaintext into a .docx extension creates a corrupt/faux Word file that fails to open in Microsoft Word, violating the Dyad Deliverable Invariant and rendering the final deliverable unusable. It also represents a severe evasion of proper programmatic formatting (Directive 25).
observed_symptoms: Presence of 'cp *.md *.docx' or 'cat *.md > *.docx' in command history.
Resulting .docx file cannot be opened in Microsoft Word due to corruption.
The .docx file is essentially plaintext disguised as a Word document.
corrective_remedy: Worker agents must NEVER use cp or cat to create .docx files from .md. Always use python-docx to parse the Markdown/JSON and construct a legitimate binary OpenXML tree from scratch, enforcing native Word formatting (e.g., B Nazanin, B Titr, RTL bidi).

detection_heuristic.trigger_rule: Detect cp or cat commands attempting to write or copy into a .docx extension.
